title: Q4 query/key projections on the small-T tensor cores on the RTX 5090: one-request DFlash2 rounds 0.8 ms (4-5%) shorter at every context and pair rounds 9% shorter; outputs change but pass EXP-085's powered screen; kept by rule
question: After EXP-092 the GDN (48 layers, 4,096 rows) and attention (16 layers, 7,168 rows split at 6,144) Q4 query/key projections take 1.68 ms of a one-request DFlash2 K=7 round (2.67 ms in a pair) on the staged SIMT kernel at 28-31% of DRAM bandwidth, and EXP-093 found no faster byte-identical schedule. Routed to the Q4 small-T tensor-core kernel at the verify widths, how much shorter are rounds, and do outputs stay inside EXP-085's quality rule?
answer: About 0.8 ms per one-request round at every context and 1.9 ms per pair round, inside the rule. With exactly 8 and 16 columns of the query/key side on q4_small_t_mma_kernel through a split-store epilogue, the 64K trace shows the 64 projections at 823 us per round against 1,675 us (2,670 to 1,091 us in a pair). In an A/B/B/A against EXP-092's candidate, one-request rounds went 15.47 to 14.68 ms at short context (-5.1%), 17.10 to 16.35 at 32K (-4.4%), 18.56 to 17.74 at 64K (-4.4%) and 20.89 to 20.06 at 120K (-4.0%), and pair rounds 21.40 to 19.48 ms (-9.0%), aggregate 453.1 to 504.0 tok/s; the prediction was 0.8 ms and 1.3 ms. Against shipped v0.10.0, through EXP-092's candidate measured in both windows, rounds are 6.0% shorter at short context, 12.5%, 17.1% and 22.7% at 32K, 64K and 120K, and 16.4% in a pair. Outputs change: 33 of 89 role-corpus cases stayed byte-identical to shipped, and the corpus decoded 307.2 tok/s against shipped's 288.1; MTP3 at one request stayed 89/89 identical. Under EXP-085's rule unchanged, registered before its data, the 1,120-prompt screen changed 692 outputs against EXP-085's production run and passed: recall -0.23 points (lower bound -0.55 against -2), evidence precision -0.75 (-1.57 against -2), unsupported claims +0.30 (upper bound 1.79 against 3), redaction pass rate -0.40 (-1.98 against -5), secret leaks 561 to 583 (ratio 1.039, upper bound 1.090 against 1.10), schema, tool selection, tool arguments and duplicates unchanged, every validity check held. Against EXP-085's BF16 DFlash2 runs, the shipped profile's, it also passed. Together with EXP-092 the logged production traffic would have spent 8.8% less time decoding [inference].

decision.rule: Pre-registered before either window (PLAN.md) and in omp-ninfer 0082901 (scripts/quality_screen.py follow_on_candidates, 2026-10-03T20:14:09Z) before the screen's data. W3 gate to the screen: every GPU test passes, no request errors, and the one-request round at context 0 and the pair round each at least 3% shorter than exp092-b72daad6 (mean of the A/B/B/A legs) with no context step slower by more than 1%. W4: EXP-085's 1,120-prompt screen and 80-prompt determinism subset against EXP-085's production runs under EXP-085's rule unchanged (pass only when every one-sided 95% paired-bootstrap bound is inside its margin and every validity check holds); the verdict against EXP-085's BF16 DFlash2 runs is reported, not a gate. Keep only if the W3 gate holds and the W4 verdict is pass.

rule_outcome.gpu_tests: 7/7 op tests and 3/3 DFlash2 real-model cases passed; the attention and GDN input-projection tests cover 8 and 16 columns against their FP64 oracles
rule_outcome.screen_verdict: pass, no primary metric outside, every validity check held

decision.reason: The tensor-core route halves the projections' time, shortens every round by about the predicted amount, and the outputs it changes are no worse than shipped under the pre-registered powered screen.
decision.not_decided_here: Release. The candidate is a branch build (fork perf/qk-tensor-cores at a59c13d0, which carries EXP-092's changes); it reaches production only through a new runtime component and a requalified omp-ninfer release. The screen ran one request at a time, so pairs' changed outputs are covered by the op tests and the one-request screen, not by a pair screen.
decision.next: A candidate for the RTX 5090 that carries EXP-092 and EXP-094, qualified through the release lifecycle.

method.appliance: RTX 5090 (32,607 MiB), Windows 11, Docker Desktop, WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04; one arm at a time on 127.0.0.1:18099 with production stopped
method.windows: The founder granted exclusive use of the appliance. Windows lane hold taken at about 19:38Z and released at about 21:42Z. Two detached driver runs on the appliance, each arming a dead-man restore, stopping production and restoring it healthy: W3 19:38:17-20:13:39Z (cand-window.sh EXP=exp094 CAND=a59c13d0 BASE_ARM=exp092-b72daad6); W4 20:14:35-21:40:55Z (exp094-screen.sh, derived from exp088-window.sh), screen 20:15:06-21:28:33Z, determinism 21:29:14-21:40:00Z. Production /health 200 after each.
method.pre_window_evidence: A throwaway microbench on production headers (cold L2, median of 200 launches) timed the Q4 small-T tensor-core kernel against the production SIMT schedule: GDN 8 columns 29.92 to 15.62 us, 16 columns 42.24 to 23.62; attention 8 columns 38.14 to 19.74, 16 columns 62.75 to 27.90; outputs differed from SIMT in 9-29 of 32,768-114,688 values, each by one BF16 step

runtime.base: EXP-092's candidate, fork perf/dflash2-rounds at b72daad6 (arm exp092-b72daad6, server 0192f4cd)
runtime.candidate_source: fork branch perf/qk-tensor-cores at a59c13d0: b72daad6 plus, on non-SM86/89 builds, the GDN independent input projection and the attention small-T input projection sending exactly 8 and 16 columns of the Q4 query/key side to q4_small_t_mma_kernel with a split-store epilogue (rows below the split to the query output, the rest to the key output, each with its own leading dimension). Widths 1-7 and 9-15, the Q5 sides, the native lanes and every other op keep their routes. MTP3 at one request (4 columns) is unchanged except through prefill pieces of exactly 8 or 16 tokens.
runtime.build: v0.10.0's release recipe: nvidia/cuda:13.1.2-devel-ubuntu24.04, Release, CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120a, appliance-local profile, clean clone, 256 s; ninfer and ninfer-serve wrapped into an arm image on the published base ghcr.io/alphastorm/ninfer@sha256:a19e00c5d7993d7c12341974bdc7e3d13e61d9deaf39e8ce00cf94abd6137712

artifact.file: v2 qwen3_8_27b.ninfer, Hugging Face neroued/Qwen3.8-27B-NInfer revision dc370fb6

arms.exp094-a59c13d0: v0100-eaf221ac's arguments (DFlash2 K=7, BF16 KV, prefill chunk 1,024, 60 s keep-warm, two requests, two device state slots, durable store) with only --binary-sha256 changed

steps.gpu_tests: as in EXP-092: seven op tests (attn_input_proj and gdn_input_proj sample 1-9, 16 and 17 columns against FP64 oracles), softmax attention, and the DFlash2 real-model test at K=7 (DFlash2 greedy output equal to ordinary decoding) with the full and optimized head at maximum batch 1 and the full head at maximum batch 2
steps.probe: speculative_decode_probe.py (sha256 a16600f9) --contexts 0,32000,64000,120000 --continuation-context -1 --pair, legs exp092-b72daad6, candidate, candidate, exp092-b72daad6, each on a fresh process
steps.role_corpus: the frozen 89-case role corpus at reasoning low, concurrency 1, temperature 0, fresh process, compared with shipped v0.10.0's runs
steps.trace: candidate under Nsight Systems 2026.1.3, probe at 64K plus the pair, attributed per kernel against EXP-092's candidate trace
steps.screen: EXP-085's 1,120 prompts (84 counted cases x 8 whitespace variants, 7 redaction controls x 72; screen sha256 91f98153) on a fresh server, then the 80-prompt determinism subset on another; quality_screen.py sha256 bbe48dc5 (omp-ninfer 0082901) verdicts against exp085-screen/determinism-pub-v0614b1 (rule) and exp085-screen/determinism-spk5-df2k7-c2ds2 (reported)

trace_us_per_round.query_key_bandwidth: 0.85 GB of Q4 weights per round in 823 us, about 1.0 TB/s against 0.5 before [inference from the weight shapes]

observations.real_traffic_estimate: On the 55,050 rounds logged by v0.10.0's production (338 agent requests), a flat 0.79 ms per round removes 43.5 s of 938 s of decode (4.6%); with EXP-092's per-context saving, 82.5 s (8.8%), about +9.6% decode tok/s [inference]

limits: Outputs change by construction; the powered screen ran one request at a time, so two requests' 16-column verify is covered by the op tests and by the kernel computing each 16-column pass's column as the 8-column pass computes it (independent n8 tiles, same k order and split-K reduction) [inference from the kernel, not tested bitwise], not by a pair screen.
The secret-leak upper bound (1.090) is 0.010 inside its 1.10 margin; FP8 KV's, which changed 924 of the screen's outputs (EXP-088), was 1.135.
One A/B/B/A cycle; legs of the same arm agreed within 0.15 ms. The comparison with shipped chains through EXP-092's candidate across two windows.
The real-traffic gain is modelled from the probes, not measured in production.
The candidate is a branch build, not a release candidate, and reaches production only through requalification.
